verdicts.reading: In 2009, as consumers focus on value, the premium for the biggest stars in the best venues erodes (megastars move from stadiums to arenas).
verdicts.reason: The chapter's own test is that megastars 'may have to play arenas, not stadiums'. In 2009 the opposite happened: U2's 360 Tour opened in stadiums, sold 650,000 tickets in seven hours, and ended as the highest-grossing tour ever ($736m, 7.27 million tickets). Grader B looked for a premium series; the chapter's stadium-versus-arena test is observable. Miss.

verdicts.reading: Quantitative (D10): in 2009 mobile advertising spend more than doubles from Deloitte's own base (US$1bn global in 2008) to over US$2bn.
verdicts.reason: The edition fixes the base: global mobile ad spend 'only $1 billion' at end-2008 (0.4% of global ad revenue). Gartner reported 2010 mobile ad revenue of US$1.6bn (forecasting more than double, US$3.3bn, for 2011), so 2009 was below US$1.6bn. 2.0 against at most 1.6 is 25% or more off: miss. Grader B's Gartner figures of US$1.7bn (2007) and US$2.7bn (2008 forecast) use an older, broader definition inconsistent with Deloitte's US$1bn base and with Gartner's own later series.

verdicts.reading: Conditional (D23): if mobile broadband demand stays strong in 2009, network and backhaul stress becomes severe.
verdicts.reason: Under D23 a conditional is graded if the condition held. Demand stayed strong (iPhone users about 400 MB a month against 40-80 MB for typical smartphones), and the stress was severe: AT&T's network in New York, San Francisco and other iPhone-heavy areas 'quickly bogged down', with failed calls and slow 3G, and AT&T invested billions and ended unlimited data in June 2010. Grader A's 'no measure of severity' is answered by the documented congestion. Hit.

verdicts.reading: The 2009 downturn hastens the demise of broadcast mobile TV in some regions (D16: within two years).
verdicts.reason: Broadcast mobile TV closed region by region: Germany's MFD ended April 2008, Albania's DVB-H ended October 2010, Austria and Switzerland switched off around 2010, the Netherlands in 2011, Finland and Italy by 2012. Closures inside the two-year window count as a hit under D16; grader A's late-timing penalty applies only from year 3. 'Temporary' turned out permanent, which does not weaken the demise. Hit.

verdicts.reading: Quantitative: worldwide mobile search revenue in 2010 is about US$1-2 billion.
verdicts.reason: No source splits 2010 mobile search exactly, but two figures bracket it. Google, the dominant mobile search provider, said in October 2010 it was on track for US$1bn in mobile revenue that year (mostly search ads, some display). Gartner put all mobile advertising at US$1.6bn in 2010, with search and maps its largest category. Mobile search therefore fell roughly between US$0.8bn and US$1.6bn, within or at most about 20% below the stated range. Grader A was right that no exact split exists, but both bracket figures are of the same quantity or contain it. Hit, low-medium confidence.
